messages:
sam: Hey all, newbie here. Ran into a weird thing with our local Postgres init scripts. I added a SQL file to docker-entrypoint-initdb.d to create extensions, but it didn't run on container start. Logs show the DB was already initialized. How do I force the init scripts to run?

erin: Welcome Sam! The docker-entrypoint-initdb.d scripts only run when the DB data dir is empty (first init). If you reused a volume that already has data, they won't run. Two options: 1) drop the named volume (`docker compose down -v`) and bring it up again so the scripts run on fresh init, or 2) run the SQL manually against the running DB with `psql` or `docker exec -it db psql -U postgres -f /path/to/script.sql`.

sam: Ahhh that explains it. I accidentally used the same named volume from another branch. If I `down -v` will I lose local dev data others might need?

jia: If the volume is shared in your compose file only on your machine, it's safe to delete. But if it's a team-shared resource (rare for local), be careful. We usually use `db_data_<username>` for dev to avoid stomping others. You can also `docker volume ls` to inspect and `docker volume rm <name>` to remove.

mike: Quick tip: for iterative dev we keep an `init/00-create-db.sql` that always runs early on first init and a `init/99-dev-only.sql` for dev fixtures. If you need to reapply schema changes without nuking data, add migration scripts to your app's migration system instead of relying on initdb.

sam: Thanks! One more related question: the app on my host uses a unix socket path in the DB URL like `postgresql:///dbname?host=/var/run/postgresql`. This worked when running the app in a container but not from host. Is there a recommended pattern?

erin: Unix sockets inside the db container are not visible to the host by default. When you run the app in a container on the same compose network you can use the service name and socket path, but host processes can't see container sockets. Map TCP ports instead and connect via 127.0.0.1, or bind-mount a host socket path (advanced, risky). We prefer mapping a high ephemeral port: `ports: - "5433:5432"` and then set host to `127.0.0.1` in your local .env.

devex-bot: Docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/local-postgres — section "init scripts & sockets". Reminder: `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` runs only on first init. See also `docker compose down -v` to remove volumes. :robot_face:

jia: Also on mac M1 chips, some Postgres images require different tags or BUILD args. If your DB exits with permission errors (`could not create lock file`) check volume ownership; named volumes usually avoid that. If you absolutely need sockets on host, you can run Postgres directly on host or use `network_mode: host` on Linux-only environments (not supported on Docker Desktop for Mac/Windows).

sam: Got it. I `down -v`ed, recreated the stack and the init SQL ran. Also switched my local app to 127.0.0.1:5433 so socket URL isn't needed. All green now, thanks everyone!

erin: Nice. Add a short note to the repo README about the `down -v` caveat so future hires don't hit the same trap. :thumbsup:
